target_customer: Software engineering teams, later regulated and sovereign buyers in defence, government, finance and healthcare
problem: Engineers spend time on routine tickets and bug fixes. Cosine built an AI software engineer to work through tickets asynchronously, and later moved to secure and air-gapped model deployments.
business_model: B2B AI software (agent and model licensing)
product_category: AI coding agent, later sovereign coding models

founders.name: Alistair Pullen
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a full-stack engineer with 15 years of experience focused on LLMs and embeddings. Education not listed.

founders.name: Yang Li
previous_startups: Ziglu (acquired by Robinhood per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Named to the 2021 Forbes 30 Under 30 per the YC page. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an agent that resolves real repository tickets in early 2023 meant working at the edge of LLM capability, with fine-tuning and codebase context retrieval. The company reported a 30 percent SWE-Bench score in August 2024 per tech.eu.

defensibility.rationale: Model capability was rented from foundation model vendors for the first product, and many teams built similar agents. Fine-tuning on curated human reasoning data was the claimed edge, which is hard to verify.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large model vendors and tool makers shipped coding agents through 2024 and 2025. No acquisition of Cosine was found. The company moved toward sovereign and secure model deployments with UK government support in 2026.

market_need_then: Developers were adopting LLM assistants in 2023 and coding was the most visible use case. Demand for autonomous ticket resolution was unproven at the time.

branding.domain_note: Company site uses cosine.sh, not a .com.

identity.logo: Wordmark, shown on a dark theme on the current site
identity.visual_style: Blue globe and point cloud graphics, technical and security oriented
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and professional, British spelling, emphasis on control and sovereignty

branding.brand_signature: Product name Genie for the agent, later replaced by the Lumen model family

rebrands.why: One analysis site says the site now leads with Lumen and Genie no longer appears; single secondary source

brand_strength.rationale: Genie drew trade press coverage after the SWE-Bench result in 2024, but the name Cosine is a generic math term and no community, mascot or merch evidence was found.

pivots.to: Sovereign coding models (Lumen) for regulated industries
pivots.why: Single secondary source describes the shift; company site now lists Lumen Sovereign trained on Isambard-AI

outcome_analysis: Cosine is still active. It raised a 2.5 million dollar seed in August 2024 after a headline SWE-Bench result, then faced heavy competition from foundation model vendors and funded agent startups. By 2026 it repositioned toward sovereign, air-gapped models with UK government compute support. Disclosed funding is small relative to its ambitions and outcome is still open.
notes: Search summaries name Sam Stenner as a third co-founder and say the company was earlier called Buildt; the YC page lists only two founders and I did not open a source confirming Stenner, so he is omitted. Competition at founding list is empty because no dated source near the W23 batch was found; tech.eu in August 2024 names Factory, Amazon Q Developer and Cognition Devin, which is later than founding. One profile reports total funding near 3 million dollars, unverified. A UK government option to join a later round was reported by IT Brief without date or amount. Founders' education not found.
